section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a path analysis testing a theoretical model linking early memories of warmth and safeness with peers, self-compassion, social safeness, body appreciation (BAS), BMI, and disordered eating (EDE-Q). The adjusted model showed significant paths: body appreciation negatively predicted disordered eating, BMI negatively predicted body appreciation and had both direct and indirect effects on disordered eating mediated by body appreciation, and early memories influenced outcomes indirectly via self-compassion and social safeness. The text does not mention multiple studies or experiments.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The proposed theoretical model was tested through a fully  saturated initial model which consisted of 27 parameters." "Body appreciation (BAS) was  showed to have a direct negative effect on disordered eating (β = − 0.60; bBAS = − 0.81; SEb = 0.05; Z = − 16.16;  p<0.001)." "BMI revealed a negative direct impact on body appreciation (β=−0.26; bBMI=−0.06; SEb=0.01; Z=−6.30; p<0.001), and a total effect of 0.40 on disordered eating which was revealed as being both direct (β = 0.24; bBMI = 0.08; SEb = 0.01; Z = 6.36; p < 0.001), and indirect, mediated by body appreciation (β=0.16; 95% CI=0.11–0.21)."

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a single path analysis testing a theoretical model linking early memories of warmth and safeness with peers, self-compassion, social safeness, body appreciation, BMI, and disordered eating. The readjusted model (Fig. 1) showed good fit and indicated that early peer warmth influences body appreciation indirectly via self-compassion and social safeness, body appreciation negatively predicts disordered eating, and BMI is negatively associated with body appreciation and has a direct positive effect on disordered eating.
section_summary.evidence_source: “The readjusted model (Fig. 1) explained 17% of self-compassion and 29% and social safeness' variances and accounted for 36% of the variance of body appreciation, and for 51% of eating psychopathology's variance.”; “BMI revealed a negative direct impact on body appreciation (β=−0.26; bBMI=−0.06; SEb=0.01; Z=−6.30; p<0.001), and a total effect of 0.40 on disordered eating which was revealed as being both direct (β = 0.24; bBMI = 0.08; SEb = 0.01; Z = 6.36; p < 0.001), and indirect, mediated by body appreciation (β=0.16; 95% CI=0.11–0.21).”

The readjusted model (single study, N = 387) showed excellent fit and significant paths: EMWSS_Peers positively predicted self-compassion and social safeness; self-compassion and social safeness positively predicted body appreciation; body appreciation negatively predicted disordered eating; BMI negatively related to body appreciation and had a direct positive effect on disordered eating. No explicit mention of multiple studies (e.g., 'Study 1') is present.
